parole.testo: From *aineh, related to Karelian aineh and Estonian aine (loan from Finnish), probably borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?], from Proto-Germanic *afniz (compare Swedish ämne (“matter, subject”)). The correspondence of Germanic *f with Finnish i may seem exceptional, but has a parallel in eine. The sens

parole.significato: harsh, hard, strict, stern [with allative ‘to’ or (partitive +) kohtaan] (of a person or character, etc.)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?], from Proto-Germanic *angazaz (compare English anger, Swedish ånger). Cognate with Karelian ankara.
ank- + -ea with a root borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?] (compare Old Norse ǫngr), or alternatively from ank- + -ea, by replacing the apparent -ra in ankara with the adjectival suffix -ea.

parole.significato: in someone's possession, custody or care
parole.testo: From *haltu- + -ssa (inessive singular), with the root borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?], from Proto-Germanic *haldaną (compare English hold, German halten, Swedish hålla).
Borrowed from Proto-Norse *ᚺᚨᛏᛏᚢᛉ (*hattuʀ) (compare Swedish hatt), from Proto-Germanic *hattuz (compare English hat). Cognate with Ingrian hattu, Karelian hattu.
Probably borrowed from Proto-Norse [script needed] (*hautr- ~ *hauþr-). Doublet of houer (“brown alga”).

parole.significato: a wide wooden dish or tub
parole.testo: Borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?], possibly with + -kka. The medial -i- is unexplained. Doublet of holkki.

parole.motivo_incerta: Uncertain; Unclear; perhaps; alternatively; modello unc/uncertain
parole.testo: Uncertain; if the earlier form was kamea, perhaps from kamala by suffix substitution (-la > -ea). Alternatively, according to Aikio (2019), derived with -ea from *kaama-, in turn borrowed from Proto-Norse [script needed] (*kāma-) (compare Icelandic kám (“dirt, muck; smudge”), Faroese kámur (“dark, m
Borrowed from Proto-Norse [script needed] (*gaistō(n)-).

parole.significato: a slippery layer or cover of ice
parole.testo: Probably borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?] (from Proto-Germanic *hēlijaz) and derived with + -ma. Cognate with Karelian kaljama.
Borrowed from Proto-Norse *ᛋᚲᚨᛚᛟ (*skalo) (perhaps more specifically from a form with -ll-, compare Old Norse skalli (“skull, a bald head”), Swedish skalle (“skull”)), from Proto-Germanic *skallô.

parole.significato: stick, billet (small, solid piece of wood, often shaped for a useful function)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Proto-Norse *ᚲᚨᛒᚢᛚᚨ (*kabula), from Proto-Germanic *kablaz; compare Swedish kavel, kavle and Norwegian kavl.
Borrowed from Proto-Norse [script needed] (*gaʀđaʀ).

parole.significato: cradle (rocking bed or cot for a baby)
parole.testo: Unknown; possibly from Proto-Norse [script needed] (*kehtō) (compare Swedish kätte (“pen, fold (for animals)”)), although LÄGLOS considers it uncertain whether such a word existed in Proto-Norse. Mostly displaced kätkyt, which remains in use in Eastern Finnish.

Borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?], from Proto-Germanic *skaidaz; compare Swedish skede (“span of time”). No cognates are found in other Baltic-Finnic languages. The original meaning "forest clearing, mound at swamp; treeless area" can still be seen in the term keidassuo. The sense of "oasis" is an a
Probably borrowed from Proto-Norse *ᛊᚲᛟᚱᛟ (*skoro), from Proto-Germanic *skurō.
Borrowed from Proto-Norse [script needed] (*gulju), from Proto-Germanic *guljō, whence Alemannic German Gülle and Swedish göl.

parole.significato: A (small) pile of hay with a hole in the middle for drying.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Proto-Norse [script needed] (*kūƀan-) (whence dialectal Swedish kuve (“haycock”)).

parole.significato: to stop, cease, come to an end, end, finish
parole.testo: Probably borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?], from Proto-Germanic *slakōną (compare *slakaz, whence slack), and derived with + -ata.

parole.significato: hair grass, tussock grass: grass in genus Deschampsia
parole.testo: Probably borrowed from Proto-Norse [script needed] (*lauha-) (compare Old Norse ló (“meadow”)).
From laup- + -ias, the root being borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?], from Proto-Germanic *laubō, *laubą (“permission, favour”).

Probably borrowed from Proto-Norse *ᛗᛟᚱᚦᚨ (*morþa), from Proto-Germanic *murþą (for *þ > *h, compare huopa), SSA however instead opines that the word may be a back-derivation from murhe, with influence in meaning from the Germanic word. If a loan, doublet of marras.
Probably borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?].
From a root nuja-, likely borrowed from Proto-Norse [script needed] (*gnūja-) (whence Swedish gny (“racket”)) + -kka. Related forms include nujertaa, nujuta, Karelian nuju (“racket, quarrel”).
Borrowed from Proto-Norse *ᛋᛒᚨᚾᚢᛉ (*spānuz) (compare Old Norse spánn) or more recently from Old Swedish spān.

parole.significato: a place to sit on by a (traditional) oven or stove
parole.testo: Borrowed from Proto-Norse [script needed] (*bankā), from Proto-Germanic *bankô; seemingly adapted with + -kko.
Possibly borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?], from Proto-Germanic *barilaz. Cognate with Karelian parilas.

parole.significato: embankment, dyke, bank (steep slope of earth, sand, etc.)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?] (compare Old East Norse *benkr), from Proto-Germanic *bankiz. Doublet of penkki, pankko, and penkka.

parole.motivo_incerta: Uncertain; Probably; perhaps; alternatively; modello unc/uncertain
parole.testo: First attested as a synonym of kaisla (since 1469); the modern sense is probably from Elias Lönnrot's Flora Fennica (1860). Origin uncertain. Perhaps borrowed from Proto-Norse *ᛒᛁᚢᛉ- (*biuʀ-), if it was a cognate of Proto-West Germanic *beusu (“rush”), but there are no North Germanic reflexes of suc

parole.significato: tail (of a bird or a marine animal)
parole.testo: Fronted from pursto, borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?], from Proto-Germanic *burstō, *burstiz (“bristle”).

parole.significato: track, railroad track (pair of formed steel rails, separated and supported usually on wooden or concrete ties or sleepe…
parole.testo: Probably raita (“stripe, streak”) + -e, or alternatively (with the same suffix) derived from Proto-Norse [Term?] (“a ride”). Compare Proto-Samic *rājδō.
Ultimately from Proto-Norse [Term?] (compare Old Norse breiða).

parole.significato: a flowing or streaming strait or sound that does not freeze even in the winter
parole.testo: Borrowed from Proto-Norse [script needed] (*straumaʀ) (compare Old Norse straumr (“stream, current”)).
Borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?] (compare Old Norse rim (“slat”)).
Probably borrowed from Proto-Norse [script needed] (*rīƀia-) (compare dialectal Swedish riv (“industrious, rapid”)) and adapted with + -eä.
Borrowed from Proto-Norse ᚱᚢᚾᛟ (runo), from Proto-Germanic *rūnō (“letter, literature, secret”), possibly from Proto-Celtic *rūnā. Compare English rune and Swedish runa.
Probably borrowed from Proto-Norse [script needed] (*hrudā) (compare Old Norse hroði (“slime”)).
Borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?] (compare Old Norse sandr, Swedish sand).
Possibly borrowed from Proto-Norse [script needed] (*sauraR).

parole.significato: seam (folded back and stitched piece of fabric)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Proto-Norse [script needed] (*saumaʀ), from Proto-Germanic *saumaz.
Cognate with Ingrian suikia. Possibly from the same root as sujua, or alternatively could be a Germanic borrowing, from Proto-Norse [Term?] (compare Old Norse svigi).

parole.significato: to fight, struggle (to contend in physical conflict; with weapons)
parole.testo: ta(k)- + -istaa + -ella, derived from a borrowing from Proto-Norse [script needed] (*taka-), compare Swedish tagas, Old Icelandic taka í mót.

parole.significato: a kind of tent or canopy held over the couple during a wedding ceremony
parole.testo: Borrowed from Proto-Norse *ᛏᛖᛚᛞᚨ (*telda), from Proto-Germanic *teldą. Doublet of teltta.
Borrowed from Proto-Norse [script needed] (*þinga), from Proto-Germanic *þingą.
Borrowed from Proto-Norse [script needed] (*dōgi(a)ʀ) (from Proto-Germanic *dōg-) and further derived with + -io.

parole.significato: accident, especially one with casualties (dead or injured)
parole.testo: Possibly borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?] (compare Icelandic tyrma (“to overwhelm”)), although disputed by LÄGLOS on the grounds that the Germanic word only has a narrow distribution and thus may not be that old. Related to Livvi turmu.
Borrowed from Proto-Norse *ᚹᚨᛗᛗᚨᛉ (*wammaʀ), from Proto-Germanic *wammaz (“spot, stain, blemish”).
vako(i)- + -ta, borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?], from Proto-Germanic *wakāną (“to wake, to be awake, to watch”).

parole.significato: to wait for, await (to expect someone to come or something to happen)
parole.testo: varro- + -ta, the root being borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?], from Proto-Germanic *wardāną.
From Proto-Norse. Compare Swedish fitta and Old Norse fytta. Cognate to Estonian vitt, Ingrian vittu, and Veps vitõińe. For sense 3, compare Russian пиздец (pizdec).

parole.significato: bail (vessel to scoop water from a boat)
parole.testo: Fronted from auskari (now rare), borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?] (compare Old Norse ausker (“bail”), Swedish öskar (“bail”)).

parole.significato: a plant of the genus Filipendula
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *angër-, possibly borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (whence Lithuanian vangarykštė) or alternatively from a hypothetical Proto-Norse [script needed] (*angan-wahstuʀ).

Uncertain, but proposed to be a Baltic loan (whence Lithuanian žaizda (“wound”)), or alternatively possibly from earlier *hagitta and then from Proto-Norse *hagiþō, compare Swedish hejd. Cognate with Karelian haitta.

From Proto-Finnic *huima (compare Estonian uim, Ingrian huima), probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic [Term?] (compare Old Norse svíma (“to faint, to swoon”)) or Proto-Norse [Term?] (compare Old Norse hvima (“to be confused”)); for sense, compare huimata. Alternatively, possibly akin to huikea (comp

parole.significato: To make a loud sound with one's voice.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *huutadak (compare Estonian hüüdma, Ingrian huutaa), either onomatopoeic, or alternatively a borrowing from Proto-Norse [script needed] (*hūta) (compare Gutnish huti (“to yell, to scream”)). * (to bid in an auction): Originally bids were shouted at auctions.

parole.significato: thick, dry and hard bark, such as that of a pine
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *karna, borrowed either from Baltic *karna- or alternatively Proto-Norse [script needed] (*skarna) (in which case related to English shear and Swedish skära).

From Proto-Finnic *kangar, *kankarëh, probably from Proto-Norse [script needed] (*gangaʀ), a later loan from the same source as kangas (“a soil type with moraine”); alternatively possibly from Proto-Uralic *këŋka- (“to climb”) (compare kangertaa). Related to Estonian kangur, Karelian kankareh and Li

parole.significato: a type of boat used to drag a seine
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *karbas, probably borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?] (compare Old Norse karfi), or alternatively and less likely from Baltic (compare Lithuanian kãrbas).
Either napa + kaira, formed after Proto-Norse *ᚾᚨᛒᛟᚷᚨᛁᛉᚨᛉ (*nabogaiʀaʀ) (from Proto-Germanic *nabōgaizaz), or directly borrowed from it.

parole.significato: stripe, band (long strip of a colour or material)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?], from Proto-Germanic *raidō, originally referring to a trail or track left behind while riding. Association with raita (etymology 2) has also been proposed. Cognate with Northern Karelian raita. Related to raide, either a derivative or a parallel loan from the same
From Proto-Finnic *rampa, borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?], from Proto-Germanic *krampaz (“curved”), or from Proto-Baltic [Term?]. If the former, doublet of kremppa.

parole.significato: shore, strand, coast (the border of a body of water and land in general)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ranta (compare Estonian rand, Veps rand), borrowed from either Proto-Norse [script needed] (*stranða), Proto-Germanic *strandō (compare Swedish strand (“beach”)) or from Proto-Baltic *kranta (compare Lithuanian krantas (“beach, shore”)).
Borrowed from Old Swedish sagh, or possibly already from Proto-Norse [Term?] (compare maha), ultimately from Proto-Germanic *sagō.

Probably either derived from dialectal tainio + -tua, from Proto-Finnic *tainijo, or directly borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?] (whence Swedish dåna). Alternatively, possibly from the same root as taipua.
Possibly from Proto-Finnic *vaanidak, probably borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?], from Proto-Germanic *wēnijaną, or alternatively possibly cognate with Erzya and Moksha ваномс (vanoms, “to look”).

parole.significato: to demand, insist, call for, order
parole.testo: Probably borrowed either from Proto-Norse [Term?] (from Proto-Germanic *wadjōną (“to wager, to pledge”)) or alternatively from Proto-Norse [Term?] (from Proto-Germanic *kwadjaną (“to greet”)). However, the -aa- (as opposed to short -a-) seems difficult to explain. Compare Karelian vuatie.
Possibly borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?], from Proto-Germanic *swinþaz (for *þ > *h, compare huopa, murha), or alternatively onomatopoeic.

parole.significato: mother (woman in relation to her children)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *äitei (compare Southern Ostrobothnian äitee, äiree, Estonian eit (“old woman”), Võro äide, äidi, ääde (“mother, grandmother”)), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *aiþį̄ (compare Gothic 𐌰𐌹𐌸𐌴𐌹 (aiþei)) or from later Proto-Norse [script needed] (*aiðijōn). Attested since the time of Mikae
